chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Tried by an Egyptian judge; near sentence of hand-cutting
summary: Butler and Chittison were tried in a tent by a judge who mocked their Western clothes; they were nearly sent to the desert but, when the Greek owner vouched for them, were fined and sentenced to pay the woman back.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Those people, they were ebony black, beautiful heads, I mean, nose -- these people they were the German -- they equalled the German race in Africa.
Tall and thin nose and thin hips and didn't shave. They did not shave. They were Sudanese. So the man knocked on my door, and didn't say ____ to me. See,

when they want you to come to them, they wave their hand away from you. I thought he was saying go away and he said you come here. So he made me know he meant for me to come. He grabbed me and so I said -- so Chitelson and I were down to the station house, so from 5:00 to 12:00 that man was writing. I don't know what had he done for all that writing to be going on but now 12:00, after they had said their prayers and everything, they took us in a big tent. We were sitting down in there, and the girls were on the sideline and the man that owned the place, the Greek that owned the place, he was there too. I think it was called the Calaise ______ or something like that.

So the judge come in, and the judge had the same type of head like Sadat, same type of head, he come in and he tried a few cases, and ______ told them to take him out of there, and then he come to Chitelson. Says ______ Chitelson, no comprehend. (unintelligible)

I don't understand. I don't stand nothing. This man said to Chitelson -- now, I know what he said, he was speaking Arab, he said, you come here with these western clothes on and want to be cute and try to fool me. You don't speak Arab. No comprende, Judge. Then he took his fez off, then he looked at me. ______. I said,
, he said, but you do speak a little bit.

He said, I know your family. Your family is the Miss family, and then he got frantic. You come here with these western clothes on and try to make a fool of me. I realized what they were saying later because they told me. He says, man beat on there with that thing, boom, boom, something like that and immediately we were -- not drug out, but picked up almost bodily and they throwed us in a little wagon and -- with a donkey in front of me, and in front of me there were two individuals and their hands were tied to a rope, and they in the cart throwed me an Chitte son up there and tied our hands.

And luckily the Greek had talked to this man and told him, 'well, these boys (unintelligible) they're Americans and they're working at Pastotis.' 'Oh, Pastotis, oh, yes, I know that man. I was getting ready to go up there. I wanted to go up there to see them.'

A man come out there frantic like, cut it, cut it, and after thought they were going to take me and Chitte son up somewhere in that beyond because they was headed for the desert and cut our hands off for stealing, because you see many people who -- their tongues have been cut off or hand has been cut off and two hands have been cut off, so that's what he had in mind for us.

And so now he took us back and rejudged us, and said this being the case, you have got to pay the woman, give her her pocketbook back and that same amount that was in the pocketbook, although she has that in there, but you pay her anyway and you pay -- and it wasn't nothing, but about $80.00 you pay it $5.00 a week.

So now we are, Chitterson and I broke the friendship, we wasn't friends any more, so I began to run by myself, with my Egyptian friends, so we would go to Cairo and go to certain places and have our fun and then come back, so what he asked me, he said, do you -- I am going to take you to my home --
